desc: Derive and prove the relationship between Manhattan distance of two boundary points and their arc-length (perimeter) positions; determine whether feasibility can be checked purely on the 1D circle of perimeter positions (e.g., dist = min(arc, P - arc) or a corrected formula), including corner cases where points are on adjacent/opposite sides.

Implement parameterization: map each point (x, y) on the boundary to a scalar position p in [0, 4*side) (e.g., going counterclockwise: bottom edge p=x, right edge p=side+y, top edge p=2*side+(side-x), left edge p=3*side+(side-y)); sort points by p.
Implement binary search on the answer d in [1, 2*side] (max possible min-distance is at most 2*side).

Implement feasibility check for a given d: for each candidate starting point (or using the sorted circular order), greedily select the next point whose position is >= current + d (wrapping around the circle, ensuring the last-to-first wrap distance also >= d); return true if we can select k points. If the 1D distance relation is not exact, incorporate direct Manhattan verification into the greedy step (e.g., advance pointer while Manhattan distance < d).

Analyze complexity (target O(n log n log(side)) or O(n k log(side)) with n <= 15000, k <= 25) and test against the three examples plus edge cases: points clustered near corners, points on the same edge, k = points.length, large side up to 1e9.

Implement the full solution: perimeter-coordinate mapping, sorted order, binary search over [0, 4*side//k], bisect/two-pointer next-array greedy feasibility with wrap-around check; verify against the three examples and edge cases (k == n, all points on one side, large side).
Assemble the final solution in the required `class Solution` format with imports (List from typing), and double-check binary search boundaries and off-by-one errors in the greedy wrap-around.
